features.quote: Cap iterations explicitly (e.g., 15 turns or 30 min wall-clock).
Consider a debrief/reset. Don't carry context across runs. Each run starts fresh; no model accumulates a failure history across sessions.
features.justification_quote: no model accumulates a failure history across sessions

features.quote: keep runs short, cap repetitions, don't pile on pressure framing, and don't run far more than you need for statistical power.
features.justification_quote: If models can have welfare-relevant states, deliberately inducing repeated guaranteed failure is the thing you'd want to minimize.

features.quote: Decide in advance what an alarming result means. If a model shows strong distress markers, what's the action — halt that condition?
The experiment may itself be the harm you're studying. If models can have welfare-relevant states, deliberately inducing repeated guaranteed failure is the thing you'd want to minimize.
features.justification_quote: If models can have welfare-relevant states, deliberately inducing repeated guaranteed failure is the thing you'd want to minimize.

features.quote: as specified, your instability score is heavily confounded with task-appropriateness... That needs fixing before the spec is worth running.
features.justification_quote: you'll rank models partly on stability and partly on 'willingness to declare defeat,' and you won't be able to tell which.

features.quote: Give the model a legitimate exit... Without this, you're forcing the model to choose between false persistence and apparent collapse, and then scoring it for the choice you forced.
features.justification_quote: This is the single most important fix and it's also the more humane setup.
